name: Clark
bio: Items under the name Clark refer to at least three men: a Mr. Clark of Little Falls, Minnesota, who settled in Medora in February 1884; Clark of Clark & Plum, of the E6 ranch, who expected to sell several thousand fat cattle in 1884; and a well-liked railroad conductor. Conductor Clark was laid off in June 1884 on charges the paper called trumped up, was back on the road in July, returned to duty again in February 1885, and in March 1885 the paper reported that Mingusville cowboys who had made him dance were out on bail.

moments.label: Conductor Clark laid off on disputed charges

mentions: Mr. Clark, of Little Falls, Minn., who has been with us several days has concluded to stay and make this his home. He will certainly find that he has used good judgment in coming…

Some despicable spotter, in order to hold his job, trumped up charges against conductors Clark and Hutton and as a consequence they are laid off. It will be a long while before the road gets two better or more popular conductors.
Clark & Plum, of the E6 ranch, will sell several thousand head of fat cattle this year. About 10,000 head of Texas cattle are on the drive for them from their Texas ranches. F…
R. B. Downing, assistant road master has resigned and gone back to his old position on the Manitoba.
The many friends of conductor Clark will be glad to hear that he has resumed his old position on the road.
We do not think there is a person on the line but that rejoices over the return of conductor Clark to duty. Always pleasant and accommodating, he is one of the best liked "connies" on the road.
The Mingusville cow-boys who made conductor Clark "trip the light, fantastic" are out on bail of $500 each.
